Map and piles on the lower screen
With touch. Does nothing on a device with one screen.
Off: 30 FPS, which saves battery and is plenty for the map and piles.
Copies each lower-screen frame to the panel on a thread of its own, so the game\'s frames don\'t wait for it. Turn off only to compare.
Updates at most one part of the lower screen per game frame, so a burst of card motion doesn\'t land in one frame up top.
Tabs you aren\'t looking at stop animating until you open them.
After that, tabs change only when you touch them.
The defaults are tuned for smooth play. Changes apply from the next launch.
Start the game once: these settings live in its settings file, which it creates on first run.
Sparks, embers and dust are drawn with fewer particles. Lighter on the GPU in busy fights; the effects stay recognisable.
As each room loads, plays its visual effects once out of sight, so the first attack of a fight does not stutter. Uses more memory and a little load time.
60 is the usual. None leaves the pace to vsync and the frame pacer, without the game\'s own limiter waiting on top, which can now and then skip a frame. Try both if fights look uneven.
Steady shows a new frame every refresh. Adaptive may drop to half rate after slow frames, to keep the pace even. Off hands frames straight to the screen. Applies on the next launch.

Saves the graphics pipelines the game compiles as it goes, instead of only when it closes cleanly, which Android seldom allows. Effects then stutter only the first time ever, not every session. Vulkan only.
Tells Android how long each frame takes, so the processor speeds up as soon as a fight gets busy instead of a few frames later. Android 13 and later; does nothing elsewhere.
Runs a full cleanup while the room transition still covers the screen, so it does not pause a fight later. Applies on the next launch.
How much new memory the game fills before a short cleanup pause. Bigger means fewer pauses in busy fights, for a little more memory. Applies on the next launch.

Reuses card and hit effects within a room instead of building each one anew, which removes the stutter as cards are played. Off: only a few effects are reused. Needs the rebuilt compat pack; applies on the next launch.
While the game loads, compiles the code for attacks, damage and effects ahead of time, so the first card of a fight does not stutter. Code only: no animations are played.
Loads common assets after the main menu and keeps them loaded between rooms, instead of loading mid-fight.
Simpler versions of the blur, fire and slash effects, made for phone GPUs. Slightly plainer effects, less GPU time.
Lower renders fewer pixels and scales up to the screen: softer, lighter on the GPU.
Smooths edges at a GPU cost; Off is recommended.
On is recommended: with the screen at 60 Hz it keeps frames evenly paced.
60 Hz matches the game\'s 60 FPS limit for even frame pacing; Highest only helps with a higher limit.
For comparison on devices where Vulkan misbehaves. The lower screen is cheaper to mirror on Vulkan.
The top screen follows whichever you used last: touch or controller. Turn off to compare.
Shows FPS and frame times over the game.
